utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But, Counsel, are you talking about Mr. Whiting's oral explanation that he gave to us on that first day of the examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So we're not talking about a written report. It was his oral account for the corrections that had been made in respect of these two statement made -- offered by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's correct. However, the submissions were made on the back of information that was gleaned during proofing, whereby, the clarification was resolved. And as -- what is typically done, the OTP provided what we call an information report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What is it that you wish to admit?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That information report where the discrepancy has been clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The written explanation report from your side?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: We haven't seen it. We've only heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I have it and the Defence has it. Perhaps we can deal with it later and I can show it to you. I can show it later, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Show it to the Defence and let it be passed to the Chamber, and we'll give a ruling on that later. Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, firstly, we did not get a number for the police report on the 22nd of November. We don't know if that document was admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted. What's the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be D56. Just for sake of clarity, we have 0471 as D54, under seal; 0479 as D55, also under seal; and now 0489 as D56, under seal as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, regarding this supplementary sheet, it was, in fact, disclosed to us but only informally. I do not believe that it can be submitted into file, and I don't think that it's really necessary, because the witness explained everything before you. I do not feel the need to have that document as evidence into file. It was not shown to the witness, neither during the examination-in-chief, neither during the cross-examination, and neither during re-examination. So this document was never shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's fine, Mr. President. I'll withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Mr. Whiting, for the next witness. Mr. Waespi, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Just before the next witness comes in, he will be taken again by Mr. Sachdeva. I have two small matters. One would require going into private session because it relates to protective measures of a witness who will testify on Wednesday. We can do it now, Mr. President, or at the end of today's court, which is in ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let's do that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, let's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Apparently, there's somebody in the public gallery. May we proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. No, I'm asking. Is it okay? Yes, we may proceed. We're in open session, and we wish to be in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The first point can be dealt with in open session, Mr. President. And it's -- it's an exhibit I have omitted to ask to be tendered as well, and it relates to Witness Kemal Buco who testified on the 2nd of February, 2007, and I have shown to the witness 65 ter number 02887, which was a report dated the 24th of November, 1994, and signed by the witness. I just forgot to ask to formally tender that exhibit. I can direct you to the lines of that exhibit, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So the 2nd of February. Today is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The 2nd of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Today is the 12th. That's some time away. I'm trying to recall it. Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not sure if this was raised in chief. I don't remember this being put to the witness. I can't even remember if I raised the issue myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When was it raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: It was raised, Mr. President, during examination-in-chief on Friday, 2nd February, and it's on pages 1493.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Which witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Kemal Buco.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Kemal Buco.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I tell you what I'll do. I'll have Chamber staff to investigate it and we will give a ruling later.. I think it is appropriate for me to tell the parties that it is their duty -- Ms. Isailovic, please listen. It is opportune for me to tell the parties that it is their duty to see that the documents they wish to have tendered are tendered. They must seek the admission of these documents. There has been negligence on the part of all parties in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It happens to the best of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just to continue the reference, it was on 1493, lines 17 to 25, and 1494, lines 1 to 8. That's where the reference was discussed and, indeed, showed the proposed exhibit to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: As I said, I'll have the Chamber staff investigate that, and we'll give a ruling on that sometime.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit. And begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, may I lead the witness through his personal details?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Knustad. I am going to, in the brief time we have left, just run through your details about your personal background. Firstly, you currently work at NATO headquarters in the United States, in Virginia, and you are military assistant to a division commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KNUSTAD.
utterances.text: That's correct. I work as military assistant to a general, which is head of a division in the NATO headquarters, in Virginia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you have been there now for six months?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KNUSTAD.
utterances.text: That's correct. I was assigned that position at the 1st of August last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And, roughly, you have spent 25 years in the Norwegian navy; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KNUSTAD.
utterances.text: That's correct. I started at the coast artillery school in 1982 and went on from there, mainly with coast artillery and artillery as my branch.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just prior to your posting in the United States at NATO headquarters, is it correct that you were the Norwegian media spokesperson for operational matters for the Norwegian forces?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KNUSTAD.
utterances.text: That's correct. I worked at the national joint headquarters in Norway as a media spokesperson, and I had the responsibility for all contacts with media on operational matters, on Norwegian national deployed forces and forces deployed abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Prior to that -- well, from 1997 to the year 2000, you were a deputy commander of the Navy Artillery School; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KNUSTAD.
utterances.text: That's correct. That's the Navy Artillery School in Norway where I served as deputy commander, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And I won't go into every single posting you've had, but is it correct that in the '80s -- in the 1980s and the early 1990s, you had various positions as gunnery commander or a gunnery officer, dealing with 155-millimetre artillery pieces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KNUSTAD.
utterances.text: That's correct. I had both education at officer training and I had service as a gunnery commander and battery commander as well, and my last assignment from before I joined the UN in 1995 was being a gunnery unit commander at coastal fortress in Norway.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Right. That's where I want to move, to the UN in 1995. Firstly, when did you join the United Nations in 1995, and where?

utterances.speaker: THOMAS KNUSTAD.
utterances.text: Well, I assigned on the 6th of June, 1995; I came from Norway to the UNMO headquarters in Zagreb where we had one week of checking in and training; and I was, after that, assigned to go to Sector Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, there we must break. And we'll adjourn until tomorrow afternoon, 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 13th day of February, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
